items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I mean the music of today I think is Elton John and the things that relate to people now

ctx.x: Can you imagine, that would be a great feeling to be a songwriter, and hear people whistling your tune.

Oh yeah, they’re really my heroes, the songwriters. I think — I really think that jazz will probably come and go, it’s a music of its time, and now I can’t see, I mean it’s silly to say now, but it’s going to go in different directions of course, and I guess people will still be playing and be inspired by it, but it’s not the music of today. I mean the music of today I think is Elton John and the things that relate to people now, country & western. I think we’re living in a less sophisticated age in terms of…
Well they certainly had a different take with romance.
